safety.intro: The BackSwitch Member Area is general information and gentle exercise. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

sections.title: Talk to your doctor or physical therapist first if:
items: You have a herniated disc, spinal stenosis, or another diagnosed spine condition.
You are not sure that it is safe for you.

sections.title: Keep your care plan
items: Do not stop or change medicines, physical therapy, injections, or any other care without talking to your doctor.
Follow your doctor's plan. This routine is meant to sit alongside it.

sections.title: Stop right away and get care if you feel:
items: Sharp pain, or pain that is getting worse.
New tingling, numbness, or weakness in your legs.
Pain that travels further down your leg.
Dizziness, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

sections.title: Call emergency services (911 in the US) if you have:
items: Loss of control of your bladder or bowel.
Numbness in the groin or inner thighs.
Back pain after a fall or an accident.
Back pain together with a fever.

sections.title: How to move
items: Move slowly, keep the range small, and never force anything.
Light effort is normal. Pain is not.
Your diary is a personal record. It is not a medical test.

triggers.name: Belly Breathing
triggers.practices: Calm, easy control of your breathing.
triggers.position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Rest one hand on your belly.
steps: Relax your shoulders and your jaw.
Breathe in slowly through your nose for about 4 seconds. Let your belly rise under your hand.
Breathe out gently through your mouth for about 6 seconds.
Keep going at a calm, easy pace for the whole minute.
triggers.feel: Your belly rising and falling. Your shoulders getting heavier and softer.
mistakes: Forcing the breath or holding it.
Lifting your shoulders with each breath.
triggers.gentle: Use shorter breaths: about 3 seconds in and 4 seconds out. Rest whenever you like.
triggers.stopIf: you feel dizzy, light-headed, or more short of breath than usual.
triggers.inst: Hand on your belly. Breathe in slowly through your nose and let your belly rise. Breathe out gently for longer. Keep your shoulders soft and your pace easy.
triggers.instGentle: Hand on your belly. Take short, easy breaths: about 3 seconds in and 4 seconds out. Keep your shoulders soft. Rest any time.

triggers.name: Gentle Pelvic Tilt
triggers.short: A small, soft rocking of your pelvis
triggers.practices: Smooth, small movement in your lower back.
triggers.position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Arms rest by your sides.
steps: Breathe out and let your lower back rest lightly toward the floor. This is a tiny movement.
Breathe in and let your back return to its natural curve.
Rock slowly back and forth, small and smooth.
Keep your legs and shoulders relaxed.
triggers.feel: A small, easy movement in your lower back and pelvis. No pinching.
triggers.gentle: Make the movement even smaller. A tiny tilt is enough.
triggers.stopIf: you feel sharp pain, pinching, or tingling in your back or legs.
triggers.inst: As you breathe out, let your lower back rest gently toward the floor. As you breathe in, return to neutral. Keep the rocking small and slow.
triggers.instGentle: Rock your pelvis in a very small, slow movement. Breathe out as you tilt and breathe in as you return. Smaller is fine.

triggers.name: Core Draw-In
triggers.short: A light activation of your deep belly muscles
triggers.practices: Gently switching on the deep muscles of your belly.
triggers.position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
steps: Breathe in naturally.
Breathe out and gently draw your belly button toward your spine. Use about one-third of your effort.
Hold for 5 seconds and keep breathing normally.
Release slowly and rest. Then repeat.
triggers.feel: A light tightening low in your belly, like a gentle hug. It is not a hard squeeze.
mistakes: Pressing your back into the floor.
triggers.stopIf: you cannot breathe normally during the hold, or you feel pain.
triggers.inst: Breathe out and gently draw your belly in, using about one-third of your effort. Hold for 5 seconds and keep breathing. Release slowly, rest, then repeat.
triggers.instGentle: Breathe out and gently draw your belly in. Hold for 3 seconds and keep breathing. Release slowly and rest, then repeat.

triggers.name: Heel Slide
triggers.short: Slide one heel while your belly stays gently active
triggers.practices: Keeping your trunk steady while a leg moves.
triggers.position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Start with your belly gently drawn in, as in the Core Draw-In.
steps: Gently draw your belly in.
Slide one heel slowly away along the floor until that leg is partly straight.
Slide it back to the start.
Switch sides. Keep your belly gently active and your hips still.
triggers.feel: Your belly keeping your trunk steady while one leg moves.
mistakes: Letting your pelvis rock or your back arch as the leg slides.
triggers.gentle: Slide your heel only a short way.
triggers.stopIf: you feel pain in your back, hip, or leg, or tingling that spreads down your leg.
triggers.inst: Gently draw your belly in. Slide one heel away along the floor, then back. Keep your hips still. Switch legs each time, slowly.
triggers.instGentle: Slide one heel just a little way and back. Keep your belly gently active and your hips still. Switch legs each time.

triggers.name: Small Bridge
triggers.short: Lift your hips just a few centimeters
triggers.practices: Glute strength with support from your belly.
triggers.position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
steps: Gently draw your belly in.
Squeeze your buttocks and lift your hips just an inch or two.
Pause for 1 to 2 seconds.
Lower slowly and repeat.
triggers.feel: Your buttocks working and your belly staying firm. No strain in your lower back.
triggers.gentle: Only squeeze your buttocks. Do not lift your hips.
triggers.stopIf: you feel pain in your back, tingling, or pain going down a leg.
triggers.inst: Gently draw your belly in. Squeeze your buttocks and lift your hips only an inch or two. Pause, then lower slowly. Keep breathing.
triggers.instGentle: Gently draw your belly in. Squeeze your buttocks without lifting your hips. Hold briefly, release, and repeat. Keep breathing.

triggers.name: Slow March
triggers.short: Lift one knee at a time with your belly gently active
triggers.position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
steps: Gently draw your belly in.
Lift one foot slowly, keeping your knee bent.
Lower it with control, then lift the other foot.
Keep your hips level and still. Breathe normally.
triggers.feel: Your trunk staying steady while your legs take turns.
mistakes: Rocking your hips from side to side.
triggers.gentle: Lift your foot only a few centimeters off the floor.
triggers.stopIf: you feel pain in your back, hip, or leg, or new tingling or numbness.
triggers.inst: Gently draw your belly in. Lift one foot slowly, then lower it and lift the other. Keep your hips level and still. Breathe normally.
triggers.instGentle: Gently draw your belly in. Lift one foot just a few centimeters, then lower it and lift the other. Keep your hips still.

firstDay.title: Check before you start
firstDay.text: Read the warning signs on the Safety page. Then confirm that none of them apply to you.

firstDay.title: Set up your space
firstDay.text: Find a flat, firm surface, like a mat or a firm bed. Wear comfortable clothes and prop your phone up where you can see it.

firstDay.title: Your first 7 minutes
firstDay.text: Do your complete first session at the Gentle level. The timer will guide you through each step.

firstDay.title: Log how you feel
firstDay.text: Rate your pain and stiffness from 0 to 10. This is the start of your personal diary.

firstDay.title: Tomorrow morning
firstDay.text: Log again when you wake up, then start day 2. You can also add a daily reminder to your phone calendar.

troubleshooting.doctorLine: If you have a diagnosed condition, check with your doctor or physical therapist first.

situations.title: Mild, occasional lower-back aches
situations.who: You feel a mild ache in your lower back now and then, and it does not stop you from your day.
adapt: Do your session every day, or whenever the ache shows up.
Take short breaks to change position during the day.
situations.skip: Nothing in particular. Skip any movement that feels uncomfortable.
situations.talk: The ache gets stronger, lasts more than a few days, or comes with other symptoms.

situations.title: Morning stiffness
situations.who: Your back feels stiff when you wake up and loosens up as you move around.
adapt: Do movements 1 to 3 in bed before you get up.
Keep each movement small. Do not push your range.
Use the "Mornings and getting up" tips in the 101 Everyday Tips.
situations.skip: Skip the Small Bridge on very stiff mornings. Do your full session later in the day.
situations.talk: The stiffness lasts a long time each morning, or it is getting worse.

situations.title: Upper-back tension
situations.who: You feel tightness between your shoulder blades or in your neck and shoulders.
adapt: Give extra time to Belly Breathing (movement 1).
Add a few breaths with soft, heavy shoulders between movements.
Use the "One-minute resets" tips for your shoulders and neck.
situations.skip: Skip any movement that makes your neck or shoulders feel tense.
situations.talk: You have pain in your chest, arm pain, or numbness in your hands.

situations.title: Sciatica-type leg pain
situations.who: You feel pain, tingling, or heaviness that runs from your back or hip down your leg.
adapt: Keep every movement small and slow.
Talk to your doctor or physical therapist about your routine.
situations.skip: Skip the Small Bridge (movement 5) if the pain travels down your leg.
situations.talk: Stop and talk to a doctor if the pain spreads further, or if you notice new numbness or weakness.

situations.title: Disc bulge or herniation (diagnosed)
situations.who: A doctor told you that you have a bulging or herniated disc.
adapt: Talk to your doctor or physical therapist before you begin.
Avoid strong bending forward, and keep every movement small.
situations.skip: Skip any movement that increases your symptoms.
situations.talk: Before you start, and again if any symptom gets worse.

situations.title: Spinal stenosis and degenerative disc disease
situations.who: A doctor told you that you have spinal stenosis or degenerative disc disease.
adapt: Talk to your doctor or physical therapist before you begin.
Do not arch your back strongly, and keep every movement small.
situations.skip: Skip any movement that increases your symptoms.
situations.talk: Before you start, and again if any symptom gets worse.

flareUp.title: Flare-up day
flareUp.intro: Some days your pain is well above your normal. That can happen. Be kind to yourself today.
steps: Do only the breathing, for about 3 minutes. Or rest.
Do not make up for it tomorrow. Continue with your normal session.
Choose the Gentle level for the next few days.
Log your pain honestly in your diary.
flareUp.talk: If the flare-up lasts more than 2 days, or if it is getting worse, talk to your doctor. Use the Safety page for warning signs.

messages.title: Welcome to day one
messages.text: Welcome. Today is about getting comfortable. Your session takes 7 minutes. Move slowly, keep every movement small, and stop if something does not feel right. The Safety page is always one tap away. Please keep following your doctor's plan.

messages.title: Keep it small
messages.text: Missed a day? That is completely fine. Just continue from today and never double up. A small, regular session is better than a big one. Pick a time that works and keep it simple.

messages.title: One week in
messages.text: You have been practicing for a week. Open your diary and look at your own notes. If you feel comfortable, you can try the Standard level. If you are not sure, stay with Gentle. There is no rush.

messages.title: Make it a habit
messages.text: Link your 7 minutes to something you already do each day, like your morning coffee or brushing your teeth. A fixed cue makes the routine easier to remember. You can also add a daily reminder to your phone calendar.

messages.title: Two weeks in
messages.text: Take a look at your chart. Notice how your numbers move from day to day. If a particular situation is on your mind, the Troubleshooting Guide has a page for it.

messages.title: Three weeks in
messages.text: Here is a tip for the week: stand up and change position every 30 minutes while you sit. Remember, if you have a day when your pain is well above normal, the Flare-up day page tells you what to do.

messages.title: One month in
messages.text: One month of practice. Take a moment to look back at your diary. If you would like to, you can tell us how your routine is going. We only share a story with your written permission.

messages.title: Keep it fresh
messages.text: Try some new Everyday Tips this week. If you are comfortable at your current level, you can also try the next level. If not, stay where you are. Your comfort comes first.

messages.title: Your guarantee window
messages.text: Your 60-day guarantee window ends in 5 days. If you would like to talk to us or ask for a refund, send an email to our support team with the email address you used to buy. There is no pressure and no questions about it.

messages.title: Day 60
messages.text: You reached day 60. Take a look at your diary and your chart. This Member Area stays open, so you can keep going at your own pace. Thank you for practicing with us.

faq.a: It is a guided 7-minute daily routine of gentle movements, with three guides and a personal diary. It is general exercise information. It is not medical advice.

faq.q: How long does a session take?
faq.a: Seven minutes. The timer guides you through one movement at a time, so you do not need to watch the clock.
No. You need a flat, firm surface like a mat or a firm bed, comfortable clothes, and your phone propped up where you can see it.

faq.q: When should I do my session?
faq.a: Any time that suits you. Many people pick the same time every day. You can add a daily reminder to your phone calendar in Settings.

faq.q: What if I miss a day?
faq.a: Just continue today. Never double up. A small, regular session is better than a long one.

faq.q: What is the difference between Gentle and Standard?
faq.a: Both take 7 minutes. Gentle uses smaller movements and shorter holds. If you are not sure, start with Gentle. You can switch any time in Settings.

faq.q: Can I use this with my doctor's treatment?
faq.a: Yes. Please follow your doctor's plan. Do not stop or change any medicine, therapy, or other care without talking to your doctor first.

faq.q: What if I feel pain during a session?
faq.a: Tap Stop right away. Light effort is normal, but pain is not. The Safety page lists the warning signs and when to get care.

faq.q: How do I move to a new phone?
faq.a: On your old phone, open Help, then Your progress, and tap Copy my progress. On your new phone, paste the text into Paste to restore.
Send an email to our support team within 60 days. Use the email address from your purchase. We will refund you. There is no pressure and no guilt.

faq.q: Who can I contact for help?
faq.a: Email our support team. You will find the address in Help. Please include the email you used to buy.
